newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end mixed in flat, lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: India shares end mixed in flat, lacklustre trade.

text.p: Major Indian stock exchanges closed mostly mixed in dull, listless trade on Friday due to lack of major market-moving news, dealers said.
The last day of the weekly settlement at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and financial year-end considerations forced major players to limit exposure, traders said.
"Quite a few players have withdrawn money from the market due to end-of-the year considerations," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Bombay's Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers.
The benchmark BSE 30-share index fell 1.85 points to end at 3,730.20. For the week it was down 12 points.
"The market outlook remains firm. We can expect a positive trend next week as local operators step up activity in the new account," said an equities dealer at a foreign brokerage.
"Foreign fund activity remains low. A consolidation at present levels will pave the way for a sustained rally," the dealer said.
Volatile price movement dissuaded funds from making fresh commitments in a big way, traders said.
"I feel the market will remain flat. Overseas buying is not coming in a big way," said Govind Agarwal, equities dealer at brokerage Motilal Oswal.
Shares of Hindustan Lever Ltd (HLL) fell after the firm announced lower than expected profits for calendar 1996, brokers said. Lever closed 0.50 rupees down at 1,008.0.
HLL said its latest results included those of Brooke Bond Lipton India which was merged effective January 1, 1996.
Net profit of the combined firm totalled 4.14 billion rupees. In 1995, profits of HLL were 2.39 billion rupees.
"The quality of earnings is not very good or in line with that of previous year," Motilal Oswal's Agarwal said. "We had been expecting a net profit of 4.7 billion rupees."
